text: I'm the Zouave of the Pont de l'Alma. Parisians read the Seine on my body. In 1910, the river reached 8.62 metres at Austerlitz. Up to my shoulders.

Could it happen again? The OECD says up to five million people affected, three to thirty billion euros of damage. Institut Paris Région: over 550,000 homes with their feet in the water. And rains like 2016 are now eighty percent more frequent.
The official maps exist. But nobody reads a prevention plan. As Yoshua Bengio says: a danger you don't see in front of you doesn't really scare you.
Meet Inès. Thirty-four, ground-floor tenant in the 12th, two kids in nursery school. 4 rue Traversière.
Open Zouave. The Seine level is live, from Hub'Eau. Say: Zouave, show me 1910. The water rises over Paris, in the official depth classes.
And your place? The camera dives to her building. One to two metres of water. Cellar flooded. Source: Paris PPRI. Then her own street.
Travel back up the river of time: 1658, 1740, 2016. Then ask: what do I do? Plan a refuge up high. Stay out of the cellar. Your children stay at school.
I've had water up to my shoulders. You don't have to. Type your address. Two minutes. And you'll know.
